iter3_vision: Deliver a verifiable commit investigation system where every quality claim is backed by deterministic infrastructure — not LLM policy. The iter-2 win (D1=0.75, D3=0.292 on n=12 panel) confirms the method works; the iter-3 redesign makes it trustworthy at scale. Script controls risk policy and quality gates; LLM generates hypotheses; Pydantic enforces schema; adversarial eval with a separate judge measures output honesty.
iter3_direction: iter-3 is the main track. Sequence: (1) extract archetype + risk_policy + quality_gate stub; (2) evidence_tagger feasibility spike; (3) wire deterministic gates; (4) fix context bundle [parallel: smart-diff]; (5) decompose monolith into HypothesisEngine; (6) THEN fix eval scoring infra (FIX-JUDGE-INFRA ∥ EXP-JUDGE-SWAP); (7) validate + n=20. Judge scoring infra is not a blocker for any refactor step — only needed before iter-3-validate D3/D5.

archived_active_tasks.name: Wrong-mechanism root cause — research, hypotheses, experiment design
archived_active_tasks.scope: Research + hypothesis space for D3 wrong-mechanism failure (91% of D3=0). No pipeline changes. Produces docs/spike-wrong-mechanism.md and defines experiment sequence.

hypotheses.H1: Symptom-first reasoning — ask observable failure before mechanism. Zero cost. Breaks abstraction-bias pattern shortcut.
hypotheses.H2: Cross-model mechanism verification — second model detects self-consistent errors. ~$0.004/commit on uncertain path.
hypotheses.H3: Historical bug RAG — TEMPORAL CONSTRAINT: corpus = closed pairs where fix_commit.date < T_investigated. Fix commit content excluded (oracle contamination). Injected label = coarse defect category derived from buggy diff only.
hypotheses.H4: Line-level evidence forcing — require +/- changed line citation for primary mechanism. Zero additional LLM cost.
hypotheses.H5: Reasoning model escalation — extended thinking on irreducible tier-1 commits. 5-10x cost on hard subset only.
hypotheses.H6: Fix-conditioned reverse analysis — show fix diff unlabeled, reverse-engineer mechanism. Eval/training insight only.
hypotheses.H8: JIT-SDP model as defect signature anchor — CodeT5+/UniXCoder fine-tuned on ApacheJIT (temporal cutoff baked into training). Produces defect_category distribution injected before HypothesisEngine. Cleaner than H3.
hypotheses.H9: Code-specific cross-model verifier — DeepSeek-Coder or Qwen2.5-Coder as verifier in H2. Architecture-independent biases ensure genuine disagreement detection.
hypotheses.H10: Code model as specialist worker in T2 Map-Reduce — Qwen2.5-Coder-7B at ~10x lower cost than Sonnet for narrow specialist lanes.

literature: Bernstein et al. NDSS 2026 — Abstraction Bias / Familiar Pattern Attack (universal across OpenAI/Anthropic/Google)
Tan et al. EMNLP 2025 — Self-Consistent Errors (voting falls below random; cross-model probe required)
Cloud RCA arxiv 2601 — RF-13 Anchoring Bias (45% lower correct prediction rate)
Anchoring study arxiv 2505 — Reasoning models: 22-35% anchoring vs 45-61% standard

CodeFlowLM arxiv 2512.00231 — CodeT5+/UniXCoder JIT-SDP fine-tuning (H8 precedent)

Qwen2.5-Coder arxiv 2409.12186 — Sonnet/GPT-4o still lead on general benchmarks; code models as verifiers
proposed_experiment_sequence: v2-d3-h1h4-symptom-first: H1+H4 on hard panel n=18 (~$0.04)
v2-d3-h3-bug-rag: Historical bug RAG if H1+H4 insufficient
v2-d3-h2-cross-model: Cross-model verification if systematic errors persist
v2-d3-h5-reasoning: Escalation for irreducible tier-1 commits
v2-d3-n20-validate: Full n=20 with best combination
open_questions: Are wrong-mechanism commits self-consistent? (same mechanism both runs?) — determines if H2 is mandatory
Does H3 RAG help or hurt? (risk of retrieval poisoning from wrong historical match) — test on hard panel n=18 first
Can extended thinking break FPA? (FPA paper: persists through explicit warning)
Is mechanism ceiling at Sonnet? (H5 + H3 attack from different angles)
Does T3 (evaluator-optimizer) converge or produce verbose re-statements of same wrong mechanism?
Does T1 (debate) require model diversity (H9) to avoid correlated-bias convergence?
What defect taxonomy for H8? (too coarse = low discriminative power; too fine = data sparsity per category)
H3 corpus quality: are ApacheJIT buggy-diff defect categories consistent enough to classify without fix info?
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: docs/spike-wrong-mechanism.md exists with problem definition, 10+ references, hypotheses H1-H10 + T1-T4 with mechanisms and costs
AC-2: Experiment sequence defined with clear dependency DAG
AC-3: Open questions listed with decision criteria
AC-4: H7 (multi-sample voting) explicitly rejected with literature justification
AC-5: H3 temporal correctness documented with valid/invalid corpus scope table

topology_hypotheses.T1: Debate pattern — two agents argue opposing mechanisms, judge decides. Requires H9 or T4 to avoid correlated biases.
topology_hypotheses.T2: Map-Reduce specialization — parallel specialist agents per defect category, reducer synthesizes. H10 for cost optimization.
topology_hypotheses.T3: Evaluator-optimizer on mechanism — internal loop critiques mechanism against H4 criteria and forces improvement.
topology_hypotheses.T4: Parallel hypothesis diversity — HypothesisEngine runs N times with diversity constraints.

execution_steps: 1. Scaffold scripts/v2_forensics_n50.py with argparse paths (--delivery-json, --run-dir, --output-json, --output-md); default paths from state.v2_failure_taxonomy
2. Load eval-iter-n50-delivery.json; build commit_index keyed by commit_prefix; assert len(results)==50
3. For each result entry, load matching investigations/{prefix}_{project}.json; merge fields per derived_fields_per_commit
4. Parse D2/D3 details with regex extractors; compute supported_count and evidence_tags from recommendations
5. Apply taxonomy_rules to assign d3_tag, d1_tag, d2_tag (+ sub_tags); record rule_id in commit.evidence for auditability
6. Optionally re-derive archetype via CommitContextBuilder+detect_archetype when data/repos available; else cap_reason fallback
8. Build hard_commit_panel: tier_1=all buggy D3=0 (expect 11), tier_2=all buggy D3=0.25 (expect 7); assert AC-6 counts
9. Emit .harness/evals/v2-forensics-n50.json; validate JSON schema (50 commits, all tags present)
10. Render .harness/evals/v2-forensics-n50.md from JSON via deterministic template (no LLM)
11. Diff priority_matrix vs state.v2_failure_taxonomy; if counts change >10%, note in meta.taxonomy_delta
12. Run script locally; verify AC-1–AC-6 programmatically (pytest test_v2_forensics_n50.py or inline assert block)
